exercise.name: 3 Point Standing Hops

reference.title: 3 Point Standing Hops (male)
reference.listing: Batch 1, exercise 8 of 10; product page viewed 2026-11-26
reference.note: Used only to identify the movement. The reference camera orbits and hides the hop directions; the left, forward, right pattern with a return to center follows the video research (JustGains page and related drills). This rig, artwork and animation are original.

exercise.laterality: Bilateral (both feet take off and land together); pattern can be mirrored

muscleNotes.calves_r: Soleus and gastrocnemius drive each rebound; in two-leg hopping the stiffness changes come mainly from the ankle.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Soleus and gastrocnemius drive each rebound; in two-leg hopping the stiffness changes come mainly from the ankle.
muscleNotes.quads_r: Absorb each landing through the small knee bend (about 20 degrees) and help the push-off.
muscleNotes.quads_l: Absorb each landing through the small knee bend (about 20 degrees) and help the push-off.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Hip extension at take-off; small at this hop size.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Hip extension at take-off; small at this hop size.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension at take-off and steady the knee on landing.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension at take-off and steady the knee on landing.
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Lift the feet clear of the floor between contacts.
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Lift the feet clear of the floor between contacts.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the knee tracking over the toes, most of all on the side hops.
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the knee tracking over the toes, most of all on the side hops.
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Keep the feet together and hip-width on the side hops.
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Keep the feet together and hip-width on the side hops.
muscleNotes.core: Light brace keeps the trunk tall and quiet so the hop comes from the legs.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the chest up against the small forward lean.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the chest up against the small forward lean.

breathing.pattern: Breathe steadily through the set and do not hold the breath. A short, light exhale on a rebound or every few hops helps keep the rhythm.
breathing.cadence: About 2 hops per second; one round of 6 hops (left, center, forward, center, right, center) takes about 3 s

prescription.work: 10–20 s per set, or 4–6 rounds of the three-point pattern
prescription.volume: Count foot contacts: about 80–100 per session across all jumping drills for beginners, 100–120 intermediate
prescription.frequency: 2–3 sessions per week with 48–72 h between hard plyometric days; more often as a light warm-up
prescription.tempo: About 2 hops per second, ground contact about 0.25 s
prescription.practice: Do one slow practice round first; there is a learning effect on similar hop tests

cues.text: Stand tall, feet hip-width, arms bent and held in front of the chest. Hop with both feet to the left point, then straight back to the center.
Hop forward and back. Land softly on the balls of the feet, knees slightly bent, then bounce straight out again.
Hop right and back. Face forward the whole time; only the feet change direction. Knees stay over the toes.
Keep the hops small and quick: think light and quiet.
Feet stay together on every take-off and landing; trunk tall, arms quiet.
Breathe steadily and keep the rhythm going round after round.

mistakes.mistake: Landing flat-footed or heels first with a loud thud
mistakes.fix: Land on the balls of the feet and let the heels lower slightly; aim for quiet contacts.
Keep a small knee bend at contact (about 10 degrees was typical in multidirectional landings).

mistakes.mistake: Knees caving inward, especially on the side hop
mistakes.fix: Push the knees out over the toes; shorten the side hop until it is controlled.

mistakes.mistake: Hops too big or too far, so each contact becomes a sink and reset
mistakes.fix: Shrink the hop; the drill is about rhythm. Wider side hops increase side-to-side ankle motion.

mistakes.mistake: Turning the hips or shoulders to face the direction of travel
mistakes.fix: Face forward the whole time, as in the hexagon test.

mistakes.mistake: Feet splitting apart or landing one foot at a time
mistakes.fix: Keep the feet together on take-off and landing.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning the trunk forward or flailing the arms
mistakes.fix: Chest up, arms bent in front, core lightly braced.

kinematics.norm: About 9–13 degrees at contact in multidirectional landings: soft, not locked

kinematics.measure: Knee flexion at the lowest point
kinematics.norm: Knee flexion amplitude about 20 degrees in repeated two-leg hopping; contact plus about 15–25 degrees (our estimate)

kinematics.setup: Ball of the foot, heel up 13° (ankle about 6° plantarflexion)
kinematics.peak: Heel lowers to 5° off the floor (ankle about 11° dorsiflexion), 17° ankle excursion
kinematics.norm: Land on the balls of the feet, heels lower slightly; ankle excursion about 19–22 degrees while loading at 2.2 Hz

kinematics.peak: 30 cm to the left, forward and right markers
kinematics.norm: About 20–40 cm (estimate; hexagon test uses 60 cm sides hopped from the center)

kinematics.peak: 2 hops per second (6 hops per round, 3 s)
kinematics.norm: Preferred rate about 2.2 hops per second, in place and hopping forward

kinematics.setup: Touchdown at 0.37 s, toe-off at 0.13 s of each hop
kinematics.peak: 260 ms contact, 240 ms in the air
kinematics.norm: About 236–268 ms at 2.2 Hz; 160–200 ms in quick single-leg lateral hops

kinematics.setup: Hip lowest at mid-contact, 13 cm below the top of the flight
kinematics.peak: Hip about 6 cm above its take-off height; feet about 9 cm off the floor at the top
kinematics.norm: Small hops; no published height for this drill. Lower hops at a fixed rate give longer contacts

kinematics.setup: Trunk about 3° forward at the bottom of a landing
kinematics.peak: about 1° in the air; pelvis never turns
kinematics.norm: Trunk tall and quiet, facing forward throughout (hexagon test protocol)

cautions: Build a base first: basic leg strength and about 30 s of single-leg balance, eyes open and closed, before jumping drills.
Do not hop with pain, acute inflammation, an acute or subacute sprain or strain, joint instability, or soon after surgery unless a clinician has cleared it.
History of stress fractures or other stress-related injury: take care and avoid unyielding surfaces. Use a firm, non-slip floor and supportive shoes.
modify: Recent ankle sprain or ankle instability: start with forward and back hops only and add the side hops later.
Older adults: two-leg hopping at 2.2–3.0 per second is feasible, but start smaller and slower.
Pregnancy, pelvic floor symptoms, osteoporosis or significant joint disease: ask a clinician first.
regressions: Quick steps to the three points instead of hops.
Forward and back only, then add the side points.
progressions: Faster rhythm with shorter ground contacts.
Slightly longer hops (up to about 40 cm).
Single-leg version once the two-foot pattern is quiet and controlled.
